title: Integrated Knowledge System
definition: A system that combines the capabilities of a content-addressed, schema-enforced DAG structure for immutable knowledge representation with a discovery, query, and social graph layer, enabling verifiable knowledge nodes to be discovered, queried, and composed across a global peer network.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a library that can store and share different types of knowledge like books and research papers. This library has a smart system that helps you find the right information easily and ensures that what you find is accurate and unchanged.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: An integrated knowledge system is a combination of a Decentralized Autonomous Graph (DAG) structure for storing and addressing immutable knowledge with a network protocol for discovery, query, and social graph. This results in a peer-to-peer network for sharing verifiable knowledge nodes.
difficulty_levels.expert: An integrated knowledge system merges the benefits of a DAG structure for content-addressed, schema-enforced knowledge representation and a distributed network protocol for discovery, query, and social graph. This leads to a verifiable knowledge graph with content addressing, schema enforcement, and peer-to-peer discovery, enhancing the integrity and accessibility of the knowledge system.

extra_fields.insight: The integration of a DAG structure for knowledge representation with a network protocol for discovery and query creates a verifiable and accessible knowledge system.
